messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P0 - AcmeCorp private connectivity: observed route blackholing for VPC-peering (eu-west-3a). Alerts triggered at 1969004321. Affected subnets: 10.200.0.0/16 -> 10.50.0.0/16. Health checks failing (30% of requests timed out). Please triage.

sophie: ack — I'm on call. pulling up telemetry now. any customer-reported impact?

customer-ops: acme reported timeouts from their web nodes to our inference endpoints. They see TLS handshakes fail and connection reset. Started ~12:04 UTC. Ticket #AC-1147.

jamal: looking at routing table dumps from our border TGW in eu-west-3. I see the peering route to 10.50.0.0/16 is present on rt-0a12 but traffic is blackholed at the AZ level. traceroute from a node in eu-west-3a -> shows first hop then * * *.

jamal: paste: ```
$ traceroute -n 10.50.12.34
traceroute to 10.50.12.34 (10.50.12.34), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  10.128.0.1  0.45 ms  0.31 ms  0.27 ms
 2  10.128.8.5  0.82 ms  0.58 ms  0.60 ms
 3  * * *
```

sophie: good signal. any change in route table timestamps? route propagation events?

jamal: checking control-plane logs — there's a flurry of route withdrawals and re-adds around 1969004300-1969004350. Looks like the cloud side did a route flap for the peering attachment in eu-west-3a.

ingrid: tagging in cloud-support. I can open a high-severity support case with provider immediately. @cloud-support can you collect attachment id + peering id and start the case?

cloud-support: on it. grabbing peering info... peering-id: pcx-0abc1234eu3, tgw-attach: tgw-attach-0f9e. Submitting case with logs and route withdraw timeline. Case #CS-98721.

sophie: we need mitigation while provider investigates. Is there a failover path? We do have a standby VPN to the customer's colo (vpn-12f). Can we shift traffic?

jamal: we have two options: 1) reprogram TGW route table to prefer TL-standby via vpn (more-specific static override) — risky but quick, or 2) ask customer to initiate connection to fallback endpoint (manual).

alex: i'm taking over the incident (handing off from sophie). oncall-bot: @alex oncall acknowledged.

oncall-bot: Handoff: previous oncall sophie -> alex. Primary SRE now alex. Paging history attached.

alex: ok. priority order: minimize customer impact -> avoid config churn -> preserve audits. jamal please prepare a config patch for a temporary more-specific route (10.50.12.0/24) to point at vpn-12f next-hop. i'll review and push after safety checks.

jamal: patch ready. preview: ```
# TGW route table rt-0a12
replace route 10.50.12.0/24 target vpn-12f --description "temp-failover-acmecorp-196900"
```

ingrid: get customer buy-in? customer-ops, can you confirm AcmeCorp will accept traffic via their VPN (they already have standby configured)?

customer-ops: confirmed — they have standby VPN active for failover. give us a heads up before cutover and we'll route their egress accordingly.

alex: prepping to apply in 5 minutes. jamal, run the impact check (dry-run) and ensure no overlap with other customers.

jamal: dry-run complete. route more-specific will match only AcmeCorp /24s and won't overlap with other peering routes. No other dependencies found.

alex: applying now.

jamal: rolled route change to TGW route table rt-0a12. command output: OK. route 10.50.12.0/24 -> vpn-12f.

customer-ops: AcmeCorp confirming connectivity improvement — packet loss dropped from 30% to ~1% on sample hosts. :thumbsup:

sophie: great. continuing to monitor. cloud-support, any updates from provider?

cloud-support: Provider replied — they saw transient control-plane instability in eu-west-3 AZ 'c' around 1969004325 and an autoscaling event triggered route reprogramming of TGW attachments. They have an RCA task in progress. Asking for our encrypted logs and BGP (if any). Provided estimated time to recover 45-60 mins.

alex: note: we didn't touch BGP on DC side (no peering BGP). This is a cloud-control-plane propagation issue. leaving temp route in place until provider confirms stable.

jamal: monitoring metrics: tcp_open_failures on our side dropped by 90% after change. latency stable. adding alert mute for this specific range to avoid noise.

ingrid: filing internal incident timeline and adding provider case link. adding runbook steps for reversion.

customer-ops: AcmeCorp wants an ETA for full resolution and rollback to original peering path. please keep them updated every 30 mins.

alex: will update every 30. next update at 1969004621. action items: (1) cloud-support follow up with provider RCA link, (2) keep temp route until stable for 1 hour, (3) coordinate rollback test with customer, (4) run post-mortem if provider confirms control-plane bug.

1969004621 alex: update: provider reports control-plane event mitigated in eu-west-3. They will monitor for 30 mins and advise rollback. No further route flaps observed after 1969004470.

cloud-support: provider: "we saw a race during TGW attach scale-up; we've deployed a fix to avoid route withdraw churn. We'll monitor and confirm." Case updated CS-98721.

jamal: starting controlled rollback test now — announcing to customer.

customer-ops: ready for test. we'll accept brief flaps during test window.

jamal: removing the temporary /24 override to let peering route take precedence. command: ```
# remove temporary
delete route 10.50.12.0/24 rt-0a12
```

jamal: removed. monitoring.

customer-ops: initial check — connectivity intact for control group, no increase in errors. Prometheus shows normal traffic.

sophie: keeping watch for 15 more mins. set alert for any new withdraw.

oncall-bot: Reminder: incident owner alex to file postmortem doc in #postmortems within 72h.

alex: will do. preliminary summary for customer: we observed transient cloud control-plane route propagation causing blackholing for AcmeCorp peering in eu-west-3a. We applied a targeted more-specific route to shift traffic to their standby VPN while provider resolved the issue. After provider fix, we performed rollback and validated traffic.

cloud-support: provider closed the high-severity case as 'mitigated' pending monitoring. CS-98721 -> status: monitoring.

alex: marking incident as mitigated at 1969005120. keeping temp notes and next steps: postmortem, confirm provider RCA link when available, review TGW autoscaling hooks in our runbooks, consider automated temporary route failover playbook for similar events.

sophie: :white_check_mark: nice work team.

customer-ops: customer acknowledges resolution and appreciates quick mitigation. closing external ticket after postmortem.

incident-bot: Incident P0 -> mitigated at 1969005120. Duration 899s. Tags: private-connectivity, vpc-peering, network-blackhole, eu-west-3
